# Optimal, LLC

> Optimal builds governed AI infrastructure for critical infrastructure. It
> engineers systems to stay resilient, deploys AI that detects AI-driven and
> other emerging threats against them, and secures the software and AI supply
> chain across the entire stack, from code and open-source packages to
> container images and AI models. Its platform, 9line, is an AI-native
> application and supply-chain security platform deployed in the client's own
> environment. Optimal is an SBA-certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small
> Business (SDVOSB). Sovereign by default.
>
> Full site content for LLM ingestion: https://gooptimal.io/llms-full.txt

## What Optimal does — three pillars

Optimal does three things that are designed to work together: it builds the
resilient foundation, it deploys AI that watches it, and it secures the supply
chain underneath it.

### Pillar 1 — Resilient, governed AI infrastructure

- **Governed AI Engineering** (signature engagement) — a Zero Trust access layer
  for AI: one authenticated gateway to every approved model, per-key virtual
  credentials and rate limits, fail-closed prompt and response guardrails,
  default-deny egress pinned to an allowlist, and a request-ID-joined audit
  trail reviewers read directly. Self-hostable and client-owned; no SDK rewrite.
- **Built to stay up.** Deployed in the client's cloud, on-premises, or fully
  air-gapped, and designed so a failure upstream degrades safely instead of
  taking critical systems with it.

### Pillar 2 — AI threat detection

- **Inline detection** on every prompt and response: direct and indirect prompt
  injection, jailbreaks, sensitive-data and secret exfiltration, and agents
  reaching for tools or resources they were never granted. Requests that fail
  are blocked fail-closed, before they reach a model or a system.
- **AI Security Assessment** — structured evaluation of AI systems, pipelines,
  and integrations against real adversary attack paths. Covers prompt trust
  boundaries, retrieval/RAG pipelines, tool- and function-call authorization,
  output handling, and secret/PII/training-data exposure. Findings mapped to the
  OWASP LLM Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS.
- **Adversarial AI Testing (red team)** — jailbreaks and system-prompt
  extraction, model and context manipulation, data and model exfiltration, and
  agent abuse / excessive-agency chains, with reproducible attack chains and the
  control that closes each one.
- **Secure AI Adoption Advisory** — usage patterns, threat models, and
  secure-adoption roadmaps scoped to the organization's risk profile.

### Pillar 3 — Supply-chain security across the entire stack

- **9line** inventories everything a system is built from: application code,
  open-source packages, container images and their OS layers, and the AI models
  in use (AI-BOM).
- **Reachability, not noise.** Vulnerability findings are enriched with EPSS
  and CISA KEV and checked for whether a vulnerable path is actually reachable,
  so teams act on what matters.
- **Evidence others can verify.** Every determination is recorded as
  machine-readable VEX that downstream teams and tools can re-derive.

## Scope boundary — what Optimal does not do

This matters for accuracy, and Optimal states it publicly:

- Optimal builds systems to stand up to an independent assessment. It does not
  perform that assessment and does not grant authorizations or issue
  certifications. Building the environment and grading it are deliberately
  separate roles.

## State, local & education (SLED)

For state agencies, counties and cities, K-12 districts, and higher education,
Optimal leads with governed AI rather than federal compliance framing: governed,
audited access to the frontier models inside the cloud the organization already
licenses; AI security assessment and governance; cloud security review and
hardening; data protection for CJIS, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and FERPA data; and IT risk
advisory. Details: https://gooptimal.io/sled

## Bring your own cloud

If a client already licenses Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud, Optimal
builds governed, audited access to the frontier models in that existing cloud —
Azure OpenAI Service (Azure and Azure Government), Amazon Bedrock (AWS), and
Google Vertex AI (GCP) — plus self-hosted models. No new vendor or procurement
required. Available to critical infrastructure operators, federal agencies, SLED
(state, local, and education), and enterprises.

## Reference pattern (Governed AI Engineering)

- Authenticated gateway — one governed endpoint to every approved model, per-key
  virtual credentials (LiteLLM), no SDK rewrite. Caller auth via Cloudflare
  Access and Okta OIDC.
- Prompt guardrails — NeMo Guardrails, fail-closed and pre-call; unit-tested
  secret and PII detectors.
- Default-deny egress — Squid allowlist proxy plus security-group enforcement;
  no configuration opt-out.
- Audit trail — structured JSON joined to Postgres by request ID; defensible
  without vendor-UI screenshots.

## Reference implementations (public, inspectable)

- **AI-Gateway** — open-source Zero Trust AI gateway reference design, the same
  pattern Optimal stands up in client environments:
  https://github.com/optimal-cyber/AI-Gateway
- **9line** — Optimal's AI-native application and supply-chain security
  platform, deployed inside a client's own environment (air-gap capable): real
  SBOM and vulnerability scanning, EPSS and CISA KEV enrichment, and
  frontier-model reachability analysis that compressed 874 raw findings to the
  18 that required action in the reference scan — every verdict carrying its
  evidence and exportable as VEX. Overview:
  https://gooptimal.io/nineline — live demonstrator: https://9line.gooptimal.io/

## Standards (engineering targets)

NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0,
NIST 800-207 Zero Trust, CISA Secure by Design, SLSA, ISO 42001.

## Common questions

**What does Optimal do?**
Optimal builds governed AI infrastructure for critical infrastructure: systems
engineered to stay resilient, AI that detects AI-driven and other emerging
threats against them, and supply-chain security across the entire stack, from
code and packages to containers and models.

**What is governed AI?**
Every use of a model is authorized, inspected, and recorded. Requests pass
through one authenticated gateway, guardrails check prompts and responses
before anything reaches a model or a system, egress is pinned to an allowlist,
and every call leaves an audit record in the client's own account.

**How does Optimal's AI detect AI threats?**
Detection runs inline on every prompt and response, catching prompt injection,
jailbreaks, data and secret exfiltration, and agent or tool-use abuse, and
blocking them fail-closed. Optimal pairs that with adversarial red-teaming
against the OWASP LLM Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS.

**Is Optimal a product company or a services firm?**
Both. Optimal is advisory-led — scoped engagements and managed operations — and
makes 9line, an AI-native application and supply-chain security platform
deployed inside the client's own environment rather than sold as multi-tenant
SaaS. The control patterns Optimal implements are published as open-source
reference architecture, so a client can read exactly what will be built and
keep operating it independently afterward.

**What is 9line?**
9line is Optimal's AI-native application and supply-chain security platform:
real SBOM and vulnerability scanning (syft, grype), EPSS and CISA KEV
enrichment, and frontier-model reachability analysis that reads the actual
codebase to determine whether a vulnerable path is reachable — turning
thousands of raw findings into an evidence-backed action queue and an
exportable VEX record. In the reference
scan it compressed 874 raw findings to the 18 that required action. It deploys
in the client's environment and is air-gap capable. Live demonstrator:
https://9line.gooptimal.io/

**What is prompt injection, and why does it matter?**
Prompt injection manipulates an AI system through crafted input, causing it to
ignore instructions, expose data, or take unauthorized actions. It is among the
most active threats to any organization deploying large language models and
agents, and it is one of the first things Optimal tests.

**Who does Optimal work with?**
Operators of critical infrastructure and the teams that build for them, across
energy and utilities, water, transportation, communications, healthcare,
financial services, the defense industrial base, and federal, state, local, and
education agencies. Optimal is an SBA-certified SDVOSB eligible for SDVOSB and
VOSB set-aside contracts, and works across commercial cloud, government cloud,
on-premises, and air-gapped networks.
